name: runtime-upgrade
title: Agent Runtime 架构升级（Workflow-centric → Kernel-centric）
creator: codex
notes:
CLOSE-OUT (2026-09-18). VERDICT: 9/9 children delivered, 51 PRs (#577-627) contiguous with no gaps. The judgement is measured, not read off the ledger: every merged PR in the window was attributed by the ticket prefix in its title, giving 51/51 attributed and the nine ticket ranges tiling #577-627 exactly. The ledger's own fields are not trustworthy in this repo -- a multi-slice ticket's task.json.commit holds only its last slice (P0/P1b/P1c/P1d hold none at all) and status still reads in_progress after delivery, so the commit graph is the only evidence. PER TICKET: P0 #577 (1) concurrent-state isolation, retry consolidation, publish idempotence, quality gate fail-closed; P1a #578 (1) ArtifactStore/EventStore/hydration + the three-layer state split; P1b #579-590 (12) recall through compile, prompt L0-L5 layering, per-agent migration, baseline gate; P1c #591-599 (9) ToolSpec + Registry + Gateway with every call site re-routed; P1d #600-605 (6) provider-native structured output; P2a #606-613 (8) PublishIntent + deterministic policy engine + human authorisation + Action Executor; P2b #614-617 (4) the lease data plane plus takeover and self-fencing plus the execution-plane contract; P2c #618-623 (6) the Plan read export, exhaustive template registry, mode/Goal convergence and the workflow.py layering; P3 #624-627 (4) the weak-label contract, its producer, and the outcome- learning contract document. TARGET STATE, COMPONENT BY COMPONENT: Agent Kernel = backend/state/**; Task Graph = state/machine.py + modes.py + docs/planning.md; Context Compiler = backend/context/**; Tool Gateway = backend/tools/runtime/**; Durable Scheduler = db/execution_leases.py + routes/_takeover.py + graph/takeover_safety.py; Decision/Action = creator_agent/policy.py + agents/nodes/publish_gate.py. Memory Fabric is the one component only half-built: the read side is unified, the write side is deliberately not (ruling 7 below). And LangGraph is only partly demoted to a Task Graph Executor -- judgement and execution moved Kernel-side, but the graph still orchestrates the mainline, which is the direct consequence of ruling 2. EIGHT REGISTERED ITEMS, NOT FIXED AT CLOSE-OUT (item (3) later found already delivered -- see CORRECTION at the end) -- closing the parent does not change their standing and does not mean they are accepted as final: (1) two publish-retry paths are neither migrated nor taken over, invisible after a restart, and they are exactly the paths a previous unfinished run would take (P2b; ranked fix list at the end of section 7); (2) the mainline still calls run_publish directly, so no PublishIntent is emitted and the policy engine is not consulted -- that half of the plan row was never built (P2a; orthogonal to the never-publish-without-authorisation property, and S5c wrote the contract down); (3) [RETRACTED 2026-09-18 -- already delivered, see CORRECTION at the end] orchestrator_router's copywriter answer for brief mode at phase=creating: the key was added by P2c-S2 (backend/graph/wiring.py:160) BEFORE this close-out was written, so the KeyError branch no longer exists. The registration was inherited verbatim from the P2c ticket, where it was still open when it was written -- it must not be read as an open item; (4) should_brief_or_optimize has no caller at all, registered in ROUTERS_WITHOUT_AN_EDGE with a reverse assertion (P2c); (5) the two text-to-JSON parsers cannot merge, because the llm_enrichment copy's raise is the only trigger for fallback_fn while de_ai_taste depends on method == algorithmic -- pinned as TestTheTwoParsersCannotBeMerged (P1d); (6) the ripple-retry route still calls RippleService directly, the tool gate deliberately covering only backend/agents/** with the boundary documented at _ALLOWED_PREFIX (P1c); (7) Memory Fabric is unified on the read side only -- merging human-gated UserFeedback with automatic weak labels would change the human gate's semantics, so it waits for a conflicting-conclusion instance (P3); (8) the refit window is the sample's creation time while the write condition is once per sync, so an old row can be labelled and still move the counter by zero -- kept deliberately, and the gate only opens once a repeated back-fill is distinguishable from a new label, because late merely delays while wrong contaminates the weights (P3, ruled in docs/outcome-learning.md section 4). WHAT THIS CLOSE-OUT DID: promoted '9 children delivered' from ledger self-report to a recomputable map (51/51 attributed, ranges tiling the window), collected the eight registered items in one place, and archived the nine children plus this parent into archive/2026-09/ per the repo's own convention. WHAT IT DID NOT DO: no production code was touched, none of the eight items was quietly fixed, and no child's prd.md or notes was edited -- archiving flips status/completedAt and moves the directory, it does not rewrite. CAVEAT ON DATES: the archive tool writes completedAt as the archival day (2026-09-18); each child's real delivery date is in its notes' DELIVERED section and in the PR range above. ONE HISTORICAL DEVIATION CORRECTED IN PLACE: P0 existed in both tasks/ and archive/2026-09/ because a previous round copied it without deleting the original; the tasks/ leftover was removed so the tree matches the tool's move semantics. completedAt for P0 keeps its original 2026-09-13.

CLOSE-OUT PR: #628 (branch chore/close-runtime-upgrade, merged as a merge commit).

CORRECTION (2026-09-18, written a few hours after the close-out itself, off a re-measurement of all eight items against the tree rather than off the registrations those items were inherited from). ONE OF THE EIGHT WAS ALREADY CLOSED WHEN THE CLOSE-OUT WAS PUBLISHED: item (3). It was carried over from the P2c ticket's own registration and P2c-S2 then resolved it inside that same ticket (PR #619, feat/p2c-s2-edges-from-plan). Measured, not read: backend/state/modes.py maps WorkflowPhase.CREATING to "copywriter" for WorkflowMode.BRIEF; backend/graph/wiring.py:160 carries "copywriter" in the orchestrator entry's answers tuple; backend/graph/routers.py:96-101 records that the router's annotation and the map are compared in both directions so they cannot drift apart again; tests/unit/graph/test_routers.py:92 pins the behaviour itself (test_brief_mode_creating_routes_to_the_copywriter), and the four graph-registry suites plus the parser suite are green together (238 passed). backend/graph/plan.py:209 states the closure outright as "Closed in S2" and records that the whole exemption mechanism was removed with it. The original item also named builder.py, which no longer holds that map at all -- it moved to backend/graph/wiring.py during P2c -- which is the fingerprint of a registration that aged out. WHY THIS MATTERS HERE MORE THAN ANYWHERE ELSE: this record's own argument is that the ledger cannot be trusted and every claim has to be re-measured from git. It applied that discipline to the nine children and then exempted itself for the eight items, taking them on trust from text someone else wrote earlier. The exemption is exactly what produced the error. THE OTHER SEVEN WERE RE-MEASURED IN THE SAME PASS AND HOLD: (1) still open -- backend/api/routes/_wf_actions.py starts its own publish-retry asyncio task and its module docstring says outright that it writes checkpoints "without taking a lease"; the only lease acquisitions are _runner.py (start_lease / end_lease) and _takeover.py, and exactly zero of them are in that retry path. (2) still open -- three direct run_publish call sites survive: backend/agents/publisher.py:480, backend/api/routes/_wf_actions.py:326, backend/api/routes/free.py:419. (4) still open -- should_brief_or_optimize occurs only as its own definition (routers.py:405), in wiring.py's ROUTERS_WITHOUT_AN_EDGE (line 348) and in the reverse assertion at tests/unit/graph/test_wiring_registry.py:257. (5) still open -- pinned by TestTheTwoParsersCannotBeMerged (tests/unit/models/test_json_parsing.py:164). (6) still open -- backend/api/routes/_wf_actions.py:92-94 still imports RippleService and calls get_instance() directly, while the tool gate's boundary is _ALLOWED_PREFIX over backend/tools/runtime only (tools/runtime/audit.py:61). (7) and (8) were not re-measured in this pass: both are design rulings from P3 written up in docs/outcome-learning.md with their reasoning and their re-open criteria, not pending defects, and no code has moved since they were recorded. NOT CHANGED BY THIS CORRECTION: no production code was touched; none of the open items was quietly fixed; the nine children's verdict is untouched (51 PRs, #577-627, still contiguous); only this record was corrected, and the original statement is left standing above it under RETRACTED so the disagreement is visible rather than edited away.
